messages:
Maria: Quick question about gateway rule precedence — if we have a host pattern like "*.redwood.ai" and a service-level header override (X-Route-Service: svc-b), should header overrides beat a more specific path match? Example config:

Maria: ```
- match: host: "*.redwood.ai", path: "/api/v1/*"
  service: svc-a
- match: host: "billing.redwood.ai", path: "/api/v1/invoices/*"
  service: svc-b
- match-header: "X-Route-Service"
  precedence: ??
```

Maria: In other words, if request to billing.redwood.ai with X-Route-Service: svc-b and path /api/v1/invoices/123 — does header override prefer svc-b even if generic host+path would match svc-a? Curious about deterministic behavior and telemetry implications.

Kevin: Short answer: we need a deterministic scoring rule. My vote: host specificity > path specificity > header override as a tiebreaker. Header-driven routing should be opt-in per route because of spoofing/caching.

Sasha: +1 to opt-in. Also think about security: headers can be injected by proxies. We should require
route.allow_header_override: true AND proxy must set x-rw-proxied: true or similar.

Jia: Important note for caches: if header can change service, caches and prefix/KV keys must include the header value (or we risk serving wrong KV cache). That impacts latency/cost. We should add explicit cache_key config if header-override is enabled.

Lucas: For rollout UX: header overrides are useful for quick canaries, but they dramatically change tracing. We should tag traces with "override.origin=header" and increment a metric so SRE can see coverage. Also, header override should be a lower precedence than exact host match — overrides should never trump an exact host+path.

Kevin: Implementation detail: compute a specificity score: exact_host=100, host_wildcard=50, path_exact=30, path_prefix=20. If header_override present add +10 only if route.allow_header_override is true. Then pick highest score. That keeps exact host wins.

Maria: That scoring idea sounds good. Can we also make it pluggable so edge teams can tweak weights per deployment?

Sasha: Yes but keep default conservative. We can expose weights in the gateway config with clear docs and a warning in Console if changed.

Jia: Tests: add unit + fuzz tests for combinations of host/path/header and ensure cache key correctness. Also add a perf test for common cases to ensure we don't regress token-level latency.

Maria: OK — I'll draft a short RFC outlining: precedence rules, opt-in header overrides, cache_key semantics, telemetry tags, and a deterministic scoring function. Anyone want to co-author? @Kevin @Sasha @Jia

Kevin: I can take the scoring section and examples.

Sasha: I'll write the security/opt-in piece and the proxy requirements.

Jia: I'll add cache and perf implications + test plan.

deploy-bot: Created issue <https://goto.redwood.ai/issue/1234|RW-GW-1234> "RFC: header-derived routing overrides and precedence" assigned to Maria.

Maria: Thanks all. I'll post the RFC draft in #eng-platform tomorrow and tag you for review. :thumbsup:
